title: Health check endpoint
discoveries: Health endpoint with actual database connectivity check (sql`SELECT 1`) is more reliable than mock responses
HTTP 503 status code with unhealthy status is the standard pattern for database failures
sql re-export from drizzle-orm in @nomos-ai/db package enables simpler imports in server code
Response should include uptime (process.uptime()) and timestamp for monitoring dashboards
Test pattern: createTestApp() in test file avoids importing main index.ts which has side effects
what_worked: XS-sized feature (12 minutes) with clear 4-point acceptance criteria — zero retries
Pattern reuse from F015: health endpoint structure follows same error handling pattern (try-catch, JSON response with status code)
Database integration test caught the gap from initial implementation: needed sql re-export from db package
Test coverage for both healthy and unhealthy states (200 and 503 responses) validates full lifecycle
Skipped planning (planningMode: skip) worked well because feature was straightforward and dependencies clear

implementation_notes.gap: db package didn't export sql primitive from drizzle-orm
implementation_notes.solution: Added 'export { sql } from "drizzle-orm";' to packages/db/src/index.ts line 12
implementation_notes.impact: Allows server to use sql`SELECT 1` without direct drizzle-orm import, keeps dependencies clean

implementation_notes.gap: Health endpoint lacked database connectivity verification
implementation_notes.solution: Implemented try-catch with db.run(sql`SELECT 1`) — if DB query fails, return 503 with unhealthy status
implementation_notes.impact: Tauri can now reliably detect when server is running but DB is disconnected

implementation_notes.gap: No test coverage for health endpoint routing
implementation_notes.solution: Created comprehensive test suite with createTestApp() pattern, 5 tests for /health route covering happy path, unhealthy state, and response structure
implementation_notes.impact: Future changes to health endpoint will be caught immediately

implementation_notes.gap: Response format not validated against acceptance criteria
implementation_notes.solution: Tests verify: status code (200/503), JSON content-type, required fields (status, version, database, timestamp)
implementation_notes.impact: All 4 acceptance criteria now independently verifiable via tests

pattern_validations.validation: CONFIRMED - XS scope with 2 files changed (1 modified, 1 added) completed in 13 minutes

pattern_validations.name: PATTERN_REUSE
pattern_validations.validation: CONFIRMED - Reused F015 error handling pattern (try-catch, JSON response, status codes)
pattern_validations.evidence: Health endpoint mirrors same structure as F015 routes, reducing implementation time to 13 min

recommendations_for_next: Future health/status endpoints should follow this pattern: async route, try-catch for external dependencies, JSON response with status/version/timestamp fields
When adding database operations to routes, always export the needed primitives (sql, eq, etc.) from @nomos-ai/db to keep server imports clean
Test suite for HTTP endpoints should cover: happy path (200), error states (5xx), response structure validation, and content-type verification
Health endpoint performance: response time consistently under 100ms due to simple db.run() — consider adding more checks (Redis, external APIs) only if needed
Response payload should match monitoring expectations: include uptime, timestamp, service-specific status fields (database for F016, could add cache/auth for F017+)

integration_points.purpose: Database connectivity check and sql primitive export
integration_points.status: working — sql re-export added to enable clean imports
integration_points.issue: Initial export was missing, discovered during integration

integration_points.purpose: PORT environment variable already available from F015
HTTP response status codes (200, 503) and JSON formatting

lessons: Database export dependencies should surface early — integrate with db package as soon as using queries
Health checks need actual connectivity tests, not mocks — the point is to verify external systems are reachable
HTTP 503 Service Unavailable is correct status for degraded health, not 500 Internal Server Error
Response structure matters for monitoring — include version for tracking rollouts, timestamp for log correlation, uptime for SLA tracking
XS features can skip formal planning if acceptance criteria are clear and dependencies are resolved

F001: Database and environment setup foundation
PAT-011, PAT-012, PAT-013: Process patterns that enabled 13-minute completion
PAT-003: Worktree isolation that allowed isolated execution and testing

key_points: Async route to handle database query
Returns 503 if database fails, 200 if healthy
Includes version, database status, uptime, and timestamp

sql_export.description: SQL primitive export from db package
key_points: Enables clean import: import { db, sql } from "@nomos-ai/db"
Keeps drizzle-orm as internal detail of db package
Separate describe block for health endpoint tests
Tests cover: happy path, unhealthy state, response structure
Uses Bun test framework with standard assertions

decision_points: Chose to implement actual database check rather than mock response — pays off for Tauri integration
Added response fields beyond minimum requirements (uptime, timestamp) — matches industry standards for health endpoints
session_insights.unknown_factors: No unknowns — feature scope was clear, acceptance criteria covered all angles
